questions.title: How do you balance throughput and latency through bulk request size?
questions.description: Determining the ideal bulk request size depends on your unique use case and the attributes of your Amazon OpenSearch Domain. Experimenting with various configurations and closely monitoring performance is recommended to find the optimal balance tailored to your specific needs

choices.title: Identify index refresh controls for optimal ingestion performance

helpfulResource.displayText: A refresh operation ensures that all updates made to an index are accessible for search. The default refresh interval is one second, indicating that OpenSearch performs a refresh every second during ongoing index writes

improvementPlan.displayText: Reducing the frequency of index refreshes (higher refresh interval) improves overall indexing performance. It's advised to set the refresh_interval parameter for all indexes to 30 seconds or longer for optimal performance

choices.title: Evaluate bulk request size

helpfulResource.displayText: Determining the optimal bulk size depends on your data, and domain configuration. However, a recommended starting point is a bulk size of 3–5 MiB per request

improvementPlan.displayText: Begin with a bulk request size of 3-5 MiB, and gradually increase the size until the indexing performance ceases to improve

content.displayText: Additional resources on improving indexing performance on OpenSearch Service clusters.

choices.title: Implement HTTP compression

helpfulResource.displayText: In Amazon OpenSearch Service domains, gzip compression can be utilized to compress HTTP requests and responses. This compression helps reduce document size, lowering bandwidth usage and latency, resulting in improved transfer speeds

improvementPlan.displayText: Use gzip compression to reduce document size, lower bandwidth usage, minimize latency, and enhance transfer speeds

choices.title: Evaluate filter_path criteria

helpfulResource.displayText: Responses from the _index and _bulk APIs carry extensive information, valuable for troubleshooting or implementing retry logic. However, due to bandwidth considerations, indexing a 32-byte document, for instance, results in a 339-byte response (including headers)

improvementPlan.displayText: Use the filter_path parameter to reduce the size of the OpenSearch Service response, but be careful not to filter out fields that you need in order to identify or retry failed requests
